q: The voltage of the wall socket is $230\,\text{V}$. How large is the peak value of the voltage?
a: $230\,\text{V}$ is the rms value, so the peak value is $U_0 = U \cdot \sqrt{2} = 230\,\text{V} \cdot \sqrt{2} \approx 325\,\text{V}$.

q: Why does the magnet rotate, and not the coil from which the electricity is taken, in a power-plant generator?
a: The flux through a stationary coil changes because of the rotating magnet in the same way as in a rotating coil, so the same alternating voltage arises. The large current is taken straight from the stationary coils to the conductors without slip rings and brushes.
